questions.q: True or false? In three-three-two, the two strikers give our team its width.
questions.explain: Right, it's false. The wide midfielders give the width, outside the two strikers.
choiceExplanations: The strikers play central. Our wide midfielders stay outside them to stretch the pitch.
Right, it's false. The wide midfielders give the width, outside the two strikers.

questions.q: Which picture splits the two striker jobs the right way?
questions.explain: Yes. One striker gives midfield a pass, and the other keeps a defender busy up high.
choiceExplanations: Nobody offers midfield a pass, so the ball has no easy way forward.
Nobody keeps a defender busy up high, so Blue's back three can step up freely.
Yes. One striker gives midfield a pass, and the other keeps a defender busy up high.

questions.q: Our right midfielder drifted inside. Where should he go to keep the team wide?
options: Into the middle, behind the strikers
questions.explain: Right. Out wide he keeps the outside route open, so the strikers keep their own jobs.
choiceExplanations: That crowds the right striker, and nobody holds the outside route.
Right. Out wide he keeps the outside route open, so the strikers keep their own jobs.
The left striker already shows there. Two players in one space means nobody is wide.
